subject: Request: dedicated capacity scheduling carveout for Novara HealthTech
messages:
From: Ethan Li <ethan.li@novara.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+procurement@novara.com
Date: 2026-09-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: dedicated capacity scheduling carveout for Novara HealthTech

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We’re close to go-live for our nightly inference pipeline (image-to-text + reranking) and have one outstanding ask around predictable latency during our critical window.

Operational details: our nightly batch runs between 02:00–04:00 UTC and spikes to ~600 concurrent requests for short 10–15 minute bursts. The primary concerns are tail latency and preemption when other tenants burst. For production stability we’d like a scheduling carveout so jobs scheduled in that window are pinned to Novara’s reserved nodes (or equivalent isolation) with a documented throughput guarantee and a fallback plan.

Can you tell us:
- Whether Redwood can offer a carveout that prioritizes our dispatch group during a fixed daily window (02:00–04:00 UTC)
- How you’d express a throughput guarantee (tokens/sec or concurrency SLA) and what levels are reasonable on our current reserved plan
- Whether maintenance or scheduler preemption can still evict workloads during that window

Attached is our current contract for reference (current_contract.pdf).

We’d like a short addendum we can present to our legal team — ideally wording we can slot into the MSA. Happy to hop on a 30-min call this week.

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Li
Head of Platform Engineering
Novara HealthTech
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated capacity scheduling carveout for Novara HealthTech

Ethan — thanks for the clear summary and the contract. We can support a scheduling carveout pattern but there are a few trade-offs I want to be explicit about before we draft addendum language. I’ve attached our internal scheduling playbook excerpt for similar carveouts (scheduling_playbook_v1.pdf).

Short answers up front:
- Yes: we can create a pinned dispatch group for your reserved GPUs and configure a daily isolation window (02:00–04:00 UTC).
- Throughput guarantee: we typically express this as reserved throughput (tokens/sec) combined with a concurrency floor for the pinned group; we’ll propose concrete numbers after Karthik reviews your peak RPS.
- Maintenance/preemption: maintenance events can be scheduled but we do not perform forced evictions during a carved-out window except for emergency security maintenance — this should be called out in the addendum.

Please confirm the exact UTC window and share: average and peak RPS during the window, and an example request size (tokens). That’ll let Karthik compute the headroom we should reserve and a practical SLA target.

Proposed next step: Karthik and I will draft addendum language and a fallback playbook; Marissa will drive contracting and legal review. Available slots for a 30-min sync: Sep 8 10:00–11:00 PDT or Sep 9 08:00–09:00 PDT.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Strategic Accounts Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ethan Li <ethan.li@novara.com>

Date: 2026-09-08T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated capacity scheduling carveout for Novara HealthTech

Ethan / team — I reviewed the pattern and ran a quick capacity sketch. A few technical notes and a first-pass SLA wording you can take to legal: see attached draft (scheduling_addendum_draft.txt).

Technical constraints and recommendations:
- Isolation model: two viable options
  1) Pinned dispatch group: exclusive assignment of your reserved instances to a named dispatch group during 02:00–04:00 UTC. Jobs from that group are scheduled ahead of general pool tasks.
  2) Priority-weighted queueing: keep shared nodes but apply a high priority score to your requests during the window; cheaper but less absolute isolation.
- Headroom and throughput: to hit a 95th-percentile tail latency target of <= 150ms for your median request (current avg ~60 tokens), we should reserve ~20% extra GPU headroom above your observed peak bursts — in numbers, with 600 concurrent short requests we’d aim for a reserved concurrency of 750 and a tokens/sec floor of ~120k for the pinned group.
- Maintenance windows: we do not schedule non-urgent maintenance that impacts carved-out windows; emergency maintenance clause should be explicit and rare.
- Fallback: if pinned nodes are unavailable (hardware failure), traffic will route to a warm standby pool with throttled concurrency and a fast-fail policy back to your origin. Include an explicit fallback route and RTO (e.g., 15 minutes to reroute).

Suggested addendum language (summary):
- Define the daily scheduling carveout window (02:00–04:00 UTC) and the named dispatch group.
- Commit to reserved concurrency and tokens/sec floor (numbers above are initial; will finalize after you share sample RPS and tokens).
- Exempt routine maintenance from that window; define emergency maintenance process and notice period.
- Enumerate fallback routing behavior and RTO/RPO targets.

I’ll be on the sync Sep 9 08:00 PDT to finalize numbers if that works.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
